title: Technological innovation for an effective energy transition in Colombia: a systematic review and scientometric analysis
objective: To map and synthesize the peer-reviewed evidence (2015-2025) on how technological advances and innovation contribute to, or are constrained in, Colombia's energy transition, combining a scientometric analysis of the field with a comparative thematic synthesis of technologies, outcomes, barriers and enablers.

research_questions.question: How has peer-reviewed research on technological innovation for the energy transition in Colombia evolved between 2015 and 2025 in volume, venues, institutions, collaboration networks and thematic clusters?

picoc.population: Peer-reviewed studies on Colombia's energy system
picoc.intervention: Technological advances and innovation for the energy transition
picoc.comparison: Over time (2015-2025) and across thematic clusters
picoc.outcomes: Publication trends, key authors and institutions, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence clusters, under-explored areas

research_questions.question: Which energy-transition technologies (non-conventional renewables, energy efficiency, storage, smart grids, microgrids, low-carbon fuels and hydrogen) have been studied for Colombia, by what methods, and what technical, economic and environmental outcomes do the studies report?

picoc.population: Colombian energy supply and demand sectors (power, industry, buildings, transport, non-interconnected zones)
picoc.intervention: Deployment, design, modelling or assessment of energy-transition technologies
picoc.comparison: Conventional fossil-based or incumbent alternatives, or between technologies, where reported
picoc.outcomes: Technical performance, cost, emissions reduction, reliability and energy access
picoc.context: Colombia, including the National Interconnected System (SIN) and the non-interconnected zones (ZNI)

research_questions.question: What barriers and enablers, including policy, regulation, finance and institutions, do the studies identify for the adoption of technological innovation in Colombia's energy transition?

picoc.population: Actors and institutions of Colombia's energy sector (government, regulators, utilities, industry, communities)
picoc.intervention: Policy instruments, regulatory frameworks (e.g., Law 1715 of 2014, Law 2099 of 2021), financing and innovation-system mechanisms
picoc.comparison: Across technologies and, where reported, against other Latin American countries
picoc.outcomes: Reported barriers, enablers and their effects on adoption

research_questions.question: What social, environmental and territorial impacts and conflicts are associated with the implementation of energy-transition technologies in Colombia?

picoc.population: Communities and territories hosting or served by energy-transition projects (e.g., La Guajira, ZNI)
picoc.intervention: Implementation of renewable, efficiency or grid projects
picoc.outcomes: Socio-environmental impacts, conflicts, acceptance, energy justice and access

inclusion.text: Colombia is the study area, or one of the cases with separately reported results
inclusion.reason: The review has national scope; multi-country studies are useful only when Colombian evidence can be isolated

inclusion.text: The study addresses a technology, technological innovation or innovation-system aspect (including policy or finance for technology deployment) related to the energy transition: non-conventional renewables, hydropower modernization, energy efficiency, storage, grids and microgrids, electrification, low-carbon fuels or hydrogen
Peer-reviewed journal article, review article or peer-reviewed conference paper
inclusion.reason: The review targets strictly peer-reviewed evidence
Covers the period after Law 1715 of 2014 and the Paris Agreement (2015) up to the last complete year

inclusion.text: Full text written in English or Spanish
inclusion.reason: Languages the review team can read and appraise

exclusion.text: Colombia is not studied, or appears only incidentally (e.g., in a list of countries or the affiliation only)
No energy-transition technology or innovation is addressed (e.g., fossil-fuel exploration or production without a decarbonization or efficiency aim, or energy mentioned only as background)
Not peer-reviewed: theses, preprints, books or chapters, technical reports, editorials, letters, conference abstracts without a full paper
Published outside 2015-2025, or the full text is in a language other than English or Spanish
Duplicate or redundant publication of a study already included (the most complete version is kept)
exclusion.reason: Avoids double counting of the same evidence

exclusion.text: Insufficient methodological or result information to extract the data items (e.g., opinion piece with no analysis)
exclusion.reason: Cannot contribute evidence to the synthesis

exclusion.text: The bibliographic record cannot be verified: authorship or venue is missing from the indexed record and cannot be confirmed, so attribution and peer-review status are uncertain
exclusion.reason: Every included study must be citable and attributable with confidence

exclusion.text: The study falls outside the reference budget of the review: after ranking all included studies by topical relation to the protocol (query, research-question and PICOC terms in title, abstract and keywords) weighted by the best SJR 2025 quartile of the journal, studies ranked past the budget of 157 included studies (200 references in total, 43 of them cited outside the included studies) are excluded
exclusion.reason: The manuscript must cite 100 to 200 references and fit 45 single-column Elsevier pages; the ranking is reproducible with review_cli.py prioritize

questions.text: Are the aims of the study clearly stated?
Is the Colombian context (region, sector, system) clearly defined?
Is the method (data, model, case or analysis) described in enough detail to be reproduced or assessed?
Are the results clearly reported and supported by the data or analysis?
Are the limitations of the study discussed?

fields.description: Study identifier shared by all reports of the same study (PRISMA 2020 reports vs studies); equals the record id when the study has a single report
Extraction depth applied to this study (see extraction.tiers)
Data, model or analytical method used
Main technical, economic, environmental or access outcomes reported, with values where available
Barriers to adoption reported by the study
Enablers, policy instruments or mechanisms that support adoption
Social, environmental or territorial impacts or conflicts reported
Gaps or future work stated by the authors

tier-1.purpose: scientometric analysis (RQ1) and mapping of technologies and headline outcomes (RQ2)

tier-2.applies_to: included studies informing RQ3 or RQ4 at full-text screening, plus any study whose full text is found during extraction to report barriers, enablers or social/environmental/territorial impacts
tier-2.fields: all tier-1 fields plus barriers, enablers, social_environmental_impacts, research_gaps
tier-2.purpose: in-depth synthesis of barriers/enablers (RQ3) and impacts (RQ4)

extraction.multiple_reports: Reports of the same study (same data, cases and scenarios) are all included and share one study_group; the study is counted once in the synthesis, and PRISMA reports both the number of reports and the number of studies.

amendments.change: Added study_group and extraction_tier fields, a two-tier extraction scheme, and a rule for multiple reports of one study.
amendments.reason: Full-text screening included 524 reports, which made uniform in-depth extraction impractical. Tiering keeps every included study in the scientometric and technology mapping and limits in-depth extraction to the RQ3/RQ4 fields, without excluding any study. Companion reports (e.g., R0006 and R0484) are linked rather than excluded as E5.
amendments.decided_after: full-text screening; no study was excluded by this amendment

amendments.change: Added technology options ocean-energy, nuclear and carbon-capture-storage, and sector option buildings-commercial-institutional.
amendments.reason: During extraction, 25 studies could only be coded technology 'other' (tidal, wave, marine-current and salinity-gradient energy; small modular reactors; CO2 capture and storage), and studies of universities, schools, hospitals and shopping centres had no matching sector option. Only studies coded 'other', 'buildings-residential' or 'multi-sector' were re-examined; no study was added or removed.

amendments.change: Added exclusion criterion E7 (unverifiable bibliographic record) and applied it to R0739, R0986 and R1661.
amendments.reason: While building the reference list, four included reports had missing authorship or venue in OpenAlex (R0739, R0762, R0986, R1661). The operator verified R0762 at its publisher (IEEE Xplore document 10037784) and kept it; the other three were excluded because their records could not be confirmed with confidence.
amendments.decided_after: data extraction and synthesis tables; 3 studies removed, 521 remain

amendments.change: Added exclusion criterion E8 (reference budget) and applied it at full text to the 364 included studies ranked past the budget of 157 (review/prioritization.json).
amendments.reason: The review line of the writing framework (papersmith 0.80.0) limits a review to 100-200 cited references and 45 single-column Elsevier pages; with 43 references cited outside the included studies, 157 included studies fit the cap of 200. Studies were ranked by topical relation to the protocol weighted by the best SJR 2025 journal quartile, not by their findings.
amendments.decided_after: data extraction and synthesis; 364 studies removed, 157 remain
